title: Northstar exec sync pre-read & action tracker
body:
Purpose: quick pre-read for the leadership (executive) weekly sync. Grounding doc — what we need to decide, data to surface, and the follow-up register so we do not leave decisions as loose TODOs.

Meeting: Exec Staff Weekly — Thu 2026-03-12 10:00-11:00 PT
Attendees (expected): CEO, CTO, Head of Product, Head of Eng, Head of Sales, Head of Ops, Head of SRE + note-taker (me)

Topline context (1 paragraph):
- Q1 demand surge continues: hosted API volume +38% month-over-month on subset of customers; Dedicated pipeline uptake accelerating. We need to: confirm capacity runway for Dedicated, approve temporary burst budget for Hosted for 2 weeks, and resolve one open SLA language gap for EU private deployments.

Key numbers to surface (bring these slides / numbers):
- Hosted API P50/P95 latency (text-gen, 2k window): 48ms / 360ms (last 7d)
- Cost per 1M tokens (hosted mix): $42 (raw infra $), targeting $35 with new batching/quantization patch
- Dedicated pool utilization (prod): 84% steady, peak 98% last Thu 09:00 PT (3 incidents in FIFO queue)
- Private onboarding pipeline: 6 customers in evaluation, 2 sign-offs pending security review

Agenda (proposed timeboxes):
- 5m quick sync & run-of-show
- 15m Capacity & risk (SRE + infra): runway, emergency burst ask, incident summary
- 20m Product prioritization: Hosted latency improvements vs Dedicated SLA/enterprise asks (decision required)
- 10m Sales escalation: top 3 logo retention risks and proposed compensations
- 5m Operations: compliance gating for EU private release
- 5m Roundtable + agree actions

Decisions needed (explicit asks):
1) Approve $150k temporary burst budget to avoid throttling of highest-value hosted customers for 2 weeks. Owner: CEO approval required.
2) Prioritize change A (KV-cache prefetch) for immediate rollout to Hosted vs prioritize Dedicated autoscaler improvements. Need product + eng tradeoff decision.
3) Approve updated SLA clause for EU Private that references region-specific uptime definitions instead of a single global target. Legal to accept updated wording.

Supporting context and tradeoffs:
- Burst budget: will buy us capacity on cloud partners with predictable short-term cost but does not solve Dedicated pressure. If denied, expect throttling on 4 enterprise customers (revenue risk).
- KV-cache prefetch (opt A): estimated 12% P95 reduction for chat workloads, low engineering effort (3 sprint-weeks). Autoscaler (opt B): medium-term fix for Dedicated peaks, higher infra complexity, 2 months.

Customer highlight (to humanize discussion):
- "CuraHealth" (mid-market, large prompt volumes, sales escalated): degraded latency during last peak; willing to sign Dedicated if we guarantee capacity for pilot. They asked for a 3-week guaranteed window in April.

Risks / open questions to surface in the meeting:
- What is the legal tolerance for region-specific SLA wording? (Legal / Compliance)
- If we push KV-cache prefetch, do we break any existing caching invariants for customers using custom prompt transforms? (Infra / Product)
- If burst budget is approved, what guardrails needed to limit spend exposure? (Finance)

Pre-reads (upload these 24h before):
- SRE incident log (last 14 days) — link in chat
- Capacity forecast spreadsheet (sheet: Capacity > Q2 runway) — see linked_artifacts
- Draft updated SLA text (legal) — Confluence draft link above

Decision register (short-lived, clear owners & due dates):
- Approve burst budget: Owner: CEO (Maya to ping), Due: 2026-03-12 EOD
- KV-cache triage / risk assessment: Owner: Lead Infra Eng (Raj Patel), Due: 2026-03-17
- Dedicated autoscaler kickoff scope doc: Owner: Head of Platform Eng (Tomás Alvarez), Due: 2026-03-19
- EU SLA final text and customer comms plan: Owner: Head of Legal (Elena Rivera), Due: 2026-03-16

Follow-ups (explicit action items to write into tickets / calendar):
- Maya: schedule 30m post-meeting working session with Finance + SRE to define burst spend guardrails (calendar invite sent).
- Raj: create short JIRA (INFRA-?) capturing KV-cache prefetch implementation plan + rollback steps. Attach perf test baseline.
- Tomás: publish autoscaler design doc stub and allocate initial eng owner(s).
- Elena: finalize SLA wording and add change summary for Customer Success to use in comms.

1:1 quick notes (for CEO / CTO 1:1s this week) — talking prompts to align ahead of exec sync:
- For CEO: emphasize revenue risk (CuraHealth) and short-term mitigation (burst budget). Ask for explicit go/no-go criteria.
- For CTO: highlight engineering tradeoff (KV-cache vs autoscaler) and ask for a recommended sequencing. Confirm resource availability.

Parking lot (not for this week unless we have time):
- Revisit pricing for ultra-low-latency tier (product + pricing model work)
- Dedicated on-prem appliance PoC timeline and cost model
- Long-term cache eviction policy research (R&D backlog)

Notes-to-self (scratchpad):
- If CEO asks for numbers on revenue impact, pull top-5 at-risk contracts and ARR exposure (Sales can provide).
- Keep the decision framing binary in the meeting: approve burst budget yes/no; pick priority A or B for engineering. Avoid open-ended asks.
- After meeting: convert register items into short JIRA tickets and ping owners in #exec-followups Slack channel.

Meeting prep checklist (30m before):
- Confirm SRE has a one-slide incident summary (P0/P1s)
- Get capacity sheet snapshot (Q2 runway) as CSV attached to the calendar
- Confirm legal has SLA draft uploaded to Confluence
- Post meeting note-taker assigned (Tomás or me)

Snapshot of follow-up timeline (high-level):
- 2026-03-12: Exec decision on burst budget and priority
- 2026-03-16: SLA text finalized and comms ready
- 2026-03-17: KV-cache risk assessment ticket created and initial tests scheduled
- 2026-03-19: Autoscaler scope doc published

Short term asks for attendees (what I want them to bring):
- SRE: one-slide incident log and capacity delta by region
- Finance: short note on acceptable guardrail thresholds for burst spend
- Legal: short note on implications of region-specific SLA variants
- Sales: list of top-5 at-risk logos and revenue exposure numbers

End of doc — keep this as the working source of truth for exec-followups. I will convert the decision register to tickets immediately after the meeting and mark this doc as "in_review" once owners confirm due dates.
